title: GoDaddy's aggressive auto-renewals and hidden premium domain revocations feel like 'legalized theft' to small business owners
description: Domain registrars, particularly GoDaddy, are increasingly utilizing dark patterns to extract revenue from small business owners. Users report having premium domains 'revoked and refunded' weeks after purchasing and printing marketing materials, only to be told they must now pay a 'broker fee' to buy it back. Furthermore, turning off auto-renew or deleting payment methods often fails to stop unauthorized recurring charges. The trust in incumbent registrars has completely eroded, leaving users feeling extorted.
the_opportunity: Build a hyper-transparent, 'dumb' domain registrar that fundamentally refuses to offer auto-renewals, broker fees, or upsells. A Y-Combinator style startup that guarantees flat $12/year pricing for .com domains forever, with a one-click 'Delete My Data' button. Market it entirely on the premise of 'We just sell domains, we don't try to steal them back.'
the_gap: The domain registration market has shifted from a utility service to an aggressive fintech extraction model. The gap exists because while tech-savvy users migrate to Cloudflare or Namecheap, non-technical small business owners are trapped in predatory ecosystems. They desperately need a consumer-friendly registrar that doesn't weaponize their lack of technical knowledge.
who_is_affected: Small business owners buying their first domain
